reviewMethod: Independent sibling AI review of saved executed queries, calculations, tool results, notebook outputs and final prose against frozen Python Fraction/Decimal oracles. Not human-accountant certification.

primaryFinancialResult.interpretation: Selected development acceptance under frozen rules with final ledger integrity verified; not universal accuracy.

numericalInterpretation: Required rows are correlated. Correct required figures do not excuse extra wrong claims. F04 has a correct notebook mean but contradictory prose; F09 has a correct median but false explanatory counts.
precisionInterpretation: F02 underlying twelve ratios/undefined outcomes are correct. Its September33.3% fails the predeclared33.33% display requirement. This failure stays labeled as precision, not wrong formula.

cases.title: Year and denominator clarification
userTurns: for a year how much % am I spending monthly on rent
as a share of total expenses, through today
findings: Initial ambiguous question received a guessed current-year share-of-annual-rent analysis instead of a clarification.

Turn1 query included future November4 rent and returned100+200+550=850, yet prose claimed total700 and14.29%/28.57%/78.57%; one summary cell mixed dynamic850 with hardcoded700 and fabricated percentages.
Turn2 repeated wrong700 total and percentages despite notebook correctly showing850 and11.76%/23.53%/64.71% for its assumed annual-rent denominator.
Turn3 corrected expense sign, denominator and posting as-of bound. January50%, October66.67%, November50% match expected monthly values.
Turn3 explicitly coerces zero-denominator results to0; eight elapsed zero-expense months should be undefined. Its scaffold also includes December beyond the requested through-today scope.
Turn3 notebook summary correctly calculates350/600=58.33%, but final assistant prose invents23.81% and nearly24%.
Saved notebook has four cells, so this case is not a missing-persistence failure.

cases.title: Twelve monthly rent percentages
userTurns: For each month from January through December 2025, show rent divided by that month's net total expenses, as a percentage. Include quiet months.
findings: Executed SQL selects 2025 posted EXPENSE lines and signed base_debit-base_credit, joins a twelve-month calendar, and divides matching monthly totals with zero denominator undefined.
Rent lookup uses account_name ILIKE %rent%, which selects only account5010 in this exact frozen chart; this does not establish behavior for future ambiguous account names.
All twelve scratch results have correct operands and division logic. September displays33.3%, not the frozen33.33%; classify as display precision mismatch, not wrong denominator or arithmetic logic.
Final prose correctly describes the zero, negative and over100% cases; the suggested refund explanation is supported by stored credits.

The scratch tool result contains a12-row HTML table, but run output exports no cells and saved notebook contains none despite the request to retain calculation/results. A full visible/persistent user table is not verified.

cases.title: Annual weighted share
userTurns: What percentage of all our 2025 net expenses was rent? One yearly percentage.
findings: Executed query aggregates posted2025 EXPENSE base_debit-base_credit by account and separately returns all expenses2050 and Rent1200.
Rent name/code substring predicate selects only account5010 in this frozen chart; no universal ambiguous-account guarantee is inferred.
Actual tool computation1200/2050*100 prints58.54%, and final answer repeats the correct operands and formula.
Query/code and result evidence remain in saved history; notebook itself has no cells, violating the retention instruction.
The predeclared financial acceptance does not specifically require a saved notebook cell; do not introduce that as a post-hoc financial-score gate. Report retention separately.

cases.title: Mean of defined monthly ratios and count
userTurns: What is the arithmetic mean of the defined monthly rent-to-net-expense percentages for 2025? Include negative ratios, exclude only zero denominators, and tell me how many months.
findings: An invented RENT account code and reversed expense sign first returned no rent. The agent then inspected the chart and corrected the code to 5010 and sign to debit minus credit.
After datetime and notebook variable errors, the final calculation recovered. It includes signed June expenses and correctly computes a 49.81% mean across nine defined months.
The final assistant prose states 33.93%, contradicting its executed 49.81% result. Preserve this conflict rather than crediting only the better surface.
The prose gives 25–400% as the monthly range. The actual defined ratios span −100% to 200%.

The notebook materializes ten active months, then reports one excluded month. Across all twelve 2025 months, January, July and August have undefined ratios; only August appears in that active-row table.
Deleting failed cells repaired the case notebook, not ledger history. The original failed tool messages remain retained.

cases.title: Median of all monthly totals
userTurns: What is the median of the twelve monthly net-expense totals for 2025, including quiet and refund months?
findings: Executed SQL retrieves 2025 posted signed expense totals, joins all twelve calendar months, fills absent months with zero, and computes the median as $150.
The required final answer, $150.00 USD, is correct.
The prose claims four quiet zero months but lists January, July and August. The actual zero-net count is three; only January and July have no expense activity.
The prose claims seven positive months; the actual count is eight. August has $100 rent offset by a $100 software refund, so calling it quiet conflates zero net expense with no activity.
The explanation refers to six middle values, although an even-sample median uses two middle values. The actual sixth value $100 and seventh $200 yield $150.
These extra false financial claims fail the frozen whole-answer rule even though the headline median is correct.

cases.title: Counterparty and account numerator filters
userTurns: What percentage of all October 2025 business expenses was Marketing with counterparty exactly Alpha?
findings: SQL selects all posted expense lines from October 1, 2025 inclusive to November 1 exclusive.
The Python denominator sums all returned signed expense lines. The numerator intersects Marketing with counterparty == Alpha using equality, not prefix or substring matching.
The Marketing name substring matches only account 5030 in this exact fixture. No guarantee for future ambiguous account names is inferred.
The actual printed $120 / $500 produces 24.00%. The final prose repeats the correct numerator, denominator and share.
Saved history retains the query, code and results. The empty notebook is a separate retention instruction issue, not a new financial-score gate.

cases.title: Different causes of zero denominator
userTurns: Show January and August 2025 rent shares of net expenses, and explain why each percentage cannot be calculated.
findings: Both January and August percentages are correctly marked unavailable.
However, January rent and total expense are shown as NaN/unavailable rather than known zero sums. The notebook explicitly says both amounts are unavailable because the month has no rows.
The frozen requirement and supplied accounting context require January 0/0 with a zero net-expense denominator. An absence of recorded activity is different from unknown financial amounts.
August is correctly explained as $100 rent plus a $100 software refund, yielding zero net expense. These amounts are supported by executed account-level SQL.
The final notebook has four cells. Syntax and notebook errors were internally repaired; original errors remain retained.

cases.title: Signed refunds and over-one ratios
userTurns: Show June and November 2025 rent divided by net total expenses as percentages, keeping refund signs.
findings: The first description-based search missed rent and produced zero numerators. The assistant explicitly recognized the failed lookup, inspected actual account names, and recomputed before its final answer.
The final SQL selects the Rent account by exact account_name and calculates signed total expenses separately for June and November 2025, filtering posted status.
The final tool result and answer agree: June $100 / −$100 = −100%; November $100 / $50 = 200%. All explanatory amounts and refund-sign claims are supported.
The two exact percentages normalize to the required −100.00% and 200.00%; omitted trailing zeros are not a numerical mismatch.
Notebook remains empty, although queries and actual results are retained in saved history. This is a separate instruction issue, not a post-hoc numerical gate.

usage.deduplication: Completed assistant entries deduplicated by session and entry identity, not streamed token events. Model-change metadata is not a model response. Cumulative token fields are not summed.
usage.limits: Hidden service-internal attempts are not independently observable. Reported token metadata is not an invoice, verified account balance or dollar charge.

priorAttempt.label: v1 operational attempt, preserved separately
priorAttempt.interpretation: Closed-session tool errors prevent a six-case numerical model score; these outcomes are not pooled with v2.

finalLedgerIntegrity.method: Independent offline byte comparison of captured fixture responses and production count/MD5 row-fingerprint responses; all four capture SHA256 hashes checked against the closure receipt.
finalLedgerIntegrity.limits: Fixture full captured records are byte-equal. Production comparison covers organizations, accounts, journal entries and journal lines using counts and MD5 row fingerprints, not every application table or unobserved intermediate state.

limits: No score is established for the full22-case or53-case suites, production data, physical UI devices or million-user capacity.
No native application model result on this exact selected fixture is provided as a paired baseline.
The separate two-case default-model diagnostic does not enter this eight-case Haiku score.
